findings.q: How many club players come back the next season, and does it differ by division?
findings.hyp: Season-to-season retention is well under 100% and lower in the women’s division, where squads are smaller and more teams fold.
findings.method: Every player on a club roster in a season (first/second teams, masters) counted as back if they appear anywhere the next season: any club, any format, GB squads included. Division = the division they mostly played that season.
findings.result: Across everyone, 75% of 1078 club players from 2025 are seen again in 2026 (provisional: the season is still being recorded). Open: 78%; Mixed: 74%; Women: 71%. Of players who missed exactly one season, 25% came back the season after (176 of 712); after two missed seasons 20% (68 of 349).
confounds: “Back” means seen at the events and squads we track. A player who dropped to a club that only plays Tour, or to pickup, counts as gone.
Roster coverage grew each year (more Instagram squad lists from 2024), so early seasons understate who was around and overstate churn.
gaps: UKU membership records would say who is still registered but not playing the tracked events.
A leaver survey for the one-season-missed group, who are the ones most likely to come back.

findings.q: Of the players who first appear in a given season, how many are still playing one, two and three seasons later, and does the club they started at change that?
findings.hyp: Most loss happens in the first year or two; players who start at a strong club stay longer (they were selected, and they get more games).
findings.method: Entry cohorts = first season seen on a club roster, 2022–2025. Survival = share seen at or after each later season. Starting club tier from the team level of their club that first season. The 2022 cohort includes everyone already playing (data starts there), so it is a mix of new and established players.
findings.result: Pooling cohorts, 76% are still playing one season on and 68% two seasons on (n=1530). top club (level 70+): 83% after one season · mid club (40–69): 84% after one season · lower club (under 40): 70% after one season.
confounds: Selection: strong clubs pick players who were already committed; the club tier is a marker, not a cause.
The 2022 “cohort” is really everyone we first saw, including long-time players; true newcomers are only separable from 2023.
Later cohorts have had less time, so pooled horizons mix cohorts.
gaps: Year each player actually started ultimate (survey or membership join date) would turn this into a real entry-cohort analysis.
University and school rosters would show the pipeline before the first club season.

findings.q: Do players leave soon after their best season, or play on past their peak?
findings.hyp: Most leavers go within a season of their peak Quality: people stop while still good, not after a long decline.
findings.method: Players with 3+ scored seasons. Peak = the season with their highest Quality. For those not seen in 2026, seasons between peak and last appearance. Anyone whose last season is 2025 is a provisional leaver: the 2026 season is still being recorded, so the “gone while good” list is the group to check on now, not a verdict.
findings.result: Of 91 leavers with 3+ scored seasons, 24% were last seen in their peak season and 60% within a season of it. 8 left in their best season with Quality 50+ (the “gone while good” group); 179 with Quality 50+ have played on 2+ seasons past their peak.
confounds: 3+ seasons is required to have a peak, so this is about players who already stayed a while.
Quality tracks the team’s results as much as the player, so a peak can be the club’s good year.
Only four scored seasons exist (2022–26), which caps how far after a peak anyone can be.
gaps: Reason for leaving (injury, moved abroad, work, family, lost interest) from an exit survey. This group is the one to ask.

findings.q: Do players who only play one kind of event drop out more than players who play the full season?
findings.hyp: Players whose season is only Tour, or only Nationals, are less attached and leave more; players who travel to European events are the most committed.
findings.method: Each club player-season classified by the events they played that year; share seen again the next season.
findings.result: Played in Europe: 86% back (n=1780) · Tour + Nationals: 70% back (n=348) · Nationals only: 64% back (n=184) · Tour / Regionals only: 63% back (n=263) · Invites only (no UKU event): 31% back (n=260)
confounds: Commitment and ability run together: the players who go to Europe are also the better players at stronger clubs.
Tour-only players include many on second teams whose next season may be at a club we track less well.
gaps: Local leagues, indoor leagues and pickup are invisible here; a Tour-only player who moves to league play looks like a leaver.

findings.q: Does the number of events a player plays in a season predict whether they come back?
findings.hyp: A dose–response: each extra event in a season raises the chance of being seen next season, with diminishing returns.
findings.method: Events played per club player-season (distinct tournaments, GB events excluded) against the share back next season.
confounds: Reverse direction: players who were already leaving play fewer events in their last season.
Event counts depend on which tournaments we hold rosters for; a club that posts no Tour squads undercounts.
gaps: Attendance at training, not just tournaments, would separate “plays a lot” from “travels a lot”.

findings.q: Do players who change clubs stay in the sport longer or shorter than players who stay put, and does the direction of the move matter?
findings.hyp: A move up keeps people in; a move down is often the step before leaving.
findings.method: Three cuts. (1) Players on a club roster in two consecutive seasons, split by whether they changed club between them, and whether they were seen a season later: both groups had the same chance to move. (2) Players with 3+ club seasons, by how many club changes they made, and whether they are still playing in 2026. (3) Every club move with both team levels known, by direction, and whether the player was seen the season after.

rows.label: Stayed at the club between two seasons: seen a season later
Changed club between two seasons: seen a season later
0 club moves (3+ club seasons): still playing
1 club move (3+ club seasons): still playing
2 club moves (3+ club seasons): still playing
3+ club moves (3+ club seasons): still playing
After a move up (stronger team): back next season
After a move level (similar level): back next season
After a move down (weaker team): back next season

findings.result: Stayed at the club: 83% seen a season later (n=1270) · Changed club: 84% seen a season later (n=292). Among players with 3+ club seasons: 0 moves: 84% still playing (n=400) · 1 moves: 89% still playing (n=233) · 2 moves: 87% still playing (n=69) · 3+ moves: 100% still playing (n=16). back after a move level: 85% (n=72) · back after a move down: 74% (n=130) · back after a move up: 91% (n=149)
confounds: Moving takes effort: people who bother to find a new club are already the committed ones, so moving is a marker of commitment as much as a cause of staying.
Moves down include relocations and life changes we cannot see.
A player who moved to a club we hold no rosters for looks like a leaver.
gaps: Why people moved (relocation, selection, friends, cost) from a short survey of recent movers.

findings.q: When players switch division, where do they go, what happens to their Quality, and do they stay?
findings.hyp: Open → Mixed is the common late-career step and extends careers; Mixed → Open/Women is the step up for improving players and costs Quality at first.
findings.method: Consecutive seasons where a player’s main club division changed (masters excluded). Mean change in Quality across the switch and share seen the season after.
findings.result: Mixed → Open: 104 players, Quality -0.2, 88% back · Open → Mixed: 81 players, Quality +8.9, 86% back · Women → Mixed: 80 players, Quality +1.1, 79% back · Mixed → Women: 74 players, Quality +9.7, 88% back
confounds: Quality is division-relative (100 = top of that division), so a switch moves the yardstick as well as the player.
Mixed squads are larger and more clubs run one, so Mixed is also where people land when their open or women’s team folds.
gaps: The reason for the switch: team folded, selection, friends, wanting to play with a partner. Ask recent switchers.

findings.q: Is dropout concentrated at the bottom (weak clubs, low Quality) or does it happen at every level?
findings.hyp: Loss is heaviest at the bottom and much lower for established players at strong clubs.
findings.method: Share back next season by the player’s club tier that season and by their Quality band.
findings.result: mid club (40–69): 82% · lower club (under 40): 70% · top club (level 70+): 82%. By Quality: under 30: 66% · 30–49: 83% · 50–69: 89% · 70+: 96%
confounds: Low-Quality players are also the ones with the least roster evidence, so some “leavers” are players we simply stopped seeing.
Quality rises with events played, which is itself a retention signal (see the dose finding).
gaps: Membership status for the under-30 group to tell lapsed from gone.

findings.q: Does the quality a club gains or loses through moves in one season predict how its rating changes the next?
findings.hyp: Net quality in (arrivals’ Quality minus leavers’ Quality) leads the club’s rating by a season.
findings.method: For each club-season with 2+ moves in or out and a rating in both that season and the next: net Quality flow against the rating change to the following season. Spearman correlation.

chart.xlabel: net Quality in through moves (season N)

findings.result: Spearman ρ = 0.11 across 78 club-seasons: a weak lead
confounds: Ratings move for many reasons (who turns up to Nationals, the field that year); moves are one input.
Most moves involve mid-Quality players, so the flow number is dominated by volume, not star power.
gaps: More seasons. Four seasons of ratings is the limiting factor here, not the method.

findings.q: Which events draw the strongest players, and how far apart are they?
findings.hyp: WUCC and EUCF sit well above Nationals, which sits above Tour; the Europe-wide tour events sit between.
findings.method: Mean Quality of the players on rosters at each kind of event (one count per player per event), 2022–2026.
findings.result: Elite Invite: 67 (n=572) · EUCF: 60 (n=1164) · WUCC: 54 (n=573) · UKU Nationals: 43 (n=2559) · Spring Tour: 42 (n=1005) · Tom's Tourney: 40 (n=640) · Summer Tour: 37 (n=1163) · Windmill: 34 (n=304) · UKU Tour / Regionals: 30 (n=2431)
confounds: Quality itself rewards finishing well at these events, so the ordering is partly built in. The size of the gaps is the information, not the order.
gaps: Game scores at Tour and Nationals would let the rating, not placings, set the level.

findings.q: Do GB squads drawn mostly from one club, or with many returning players, finish higher?
findings.hyp: A core from one strong club (shared systems) and more returning caps both help; squads spread thinly across many clubs finish lower.
findings.method: Every GB squad with 10+ known players and a finish: share from the single biggest club, number of clubs, share of new caps, against finishing place (lower is better). Spearman within senior, U24 and junior lines.

chart.xlabel: share of squad from its biggest club

findings.result: Senior: ρ(top-club share, place) = -0.49, ρ(new caps, place) = -0.12 over 6 squads · U24: ρ(top-club share, place) = -0.36, ρ(new caps, place) = 0.38 over 6 squads. Negative ρ = more concentration / more new caps goes with a better finish.
confounds: One squad per edition: n is tiny and the field changes every time (Worlds vs Euros, who else entered).
Club share is read from the squad list’s club column, which is missing for many older squads.
gaps: Game-by-game results for GB squads (WFDF has them) would replace a single place with a strength measure.

findings.q: How old are GB youth products when they reach a senior squad, and when they stop playing?
findings.hyp: Youth entrants reach senior squads around 22–25 and most are gone from the tracked game by 30.
findings.method: No birthdates exist in the data. Eligibility gives hard limits (Max, 17 Oct 2026): a U17, U20 or U24 player turns at most 17, 20 or 24 that year, so is born in or after year − 17/20/24; a masters player turns at least 30 (women) or 33 (men) that year. For GB youth players the squad age band gives a birth year to within ±1–2 years (narrowed when they appear in more than one youth squad); ages below use the midpoint. Across the data, 681 players have a youth-squad floor and 795 a masters ceiling; 15 have both, and none are impossible (an impossible pair would mean two people sharing a name).

keys.name: Age at first senior GB squad
Age of those still playing in 2026

findings.result: 750 players have a birth-year estimate. Median age at first senior squad 23 (n=100); median age when last seen, for those who reached club ultimate and have gone since 2022, 26 (n=79); those still playing club ultimate are a median 24 (n=267).
confounds: Only GB youth products have an estimate, and they are the most committed players of their age; this says nothing about the typical club player’s age.
The estimate is ±2 years for most players.
gaps: Birth year (or even age band) on membership would allow relative-age-effect analysis across the whole sport: the standard talent-development question, which we cannot touch today.

findings.q: Do GB players stay in the sport more than club players of the same standard?
findings.hyp: GB selection adds commitment beyond ability: at the same Quality band, GB players come back more.
findings.method: Share back next season by Quality band, split by whether the player had been in any GB squad by that season.

keys.key: GB squad that year or before
keys.name: Has been in a GB squad

findings.result: under 30: GB 86% vs non-GB 65% · 30–49: GB 84% vs non-GB 82% · 50–69: GB 92% vs non-GB 87% · 70+: GB 97% vs non-GB 93%
confounds: Quality includes a GB selection term, so GB players sit higher in a band by construction.
GB players have more roster evidence (squad pages), so they are easier to “see” next season.
gaps: Training-squad and trial lists would add the players who tried for GB and were not picked: the right comparison group.

findings.q: How big is each stage of the pipeline: youth teams, club teams, rostered players, GB youth squads?
findings.hyp: The club game is fed by a youth base we barely see and a large university game we see only as teams.
findings.method: Counts per year (2022 on, where rosters exist) of distinct teams at UKU Youth events, distinct UK club teams at UKU events, distinct players on club rosters, and GB U17/U20 squads.

head: Year
Youth teams (UKU Youth)
University teams (indoor, season ending that year)
Club teams at UKU events
Players on club rosters
GB U17/U20 squads

findings.result: 2026: 16 youth teams, 256 university indoor teams, 77 club teams, 1320 rostered players. University teams are now counted, but without players nobody can be followed from university into the club game: that is where most sports lose the most players.
confounds: Youth results only run from 2021 and name teams, not players, so nobody can be followed from youth to club.
Club team counts depend on which events we hold standings for each year.
gaps: BUCS results and university squad lists.
UKU Youth rosters, or even a count of registered junior players per year.
Membership numbers by age band and region from UKU: the one dataset that would size every stage.

findings.q: Do university players who also play club while at university stay in the sport after they graduate?
findings.hyp: University is a drop-off point: players who only ever play university ultimate mostly stop when they leave, while those who already touch the club game carry on.
findings.method: Named squads for Bath, Exeter, KCL, Leeds, Loughborough from their Instagram posts (championships, BUCS, club events entered as the university). University years = seasons on those squads. "Club while at university" = a club roster or club event in those years, or the university team entering a club event (beginners events excluded). "Seen after" = any club, GB or community activity after the summer of their last university season. Only players whose last season ended before 2026 are judged.
findings.result: Seen in the sport after university: 21 of 42 (50%) who played club while at university, against 11 of 260 (4%) who only played university ultimate. The gap holds at every university with enough leavers. By the best university team reached: 1s 29 of 153 (19%) · 2s 3 of 67 (4%) · 3s and below 0 of 82 (0%).
confounds: Selection: keener players do both; club play is a marker of commitment as much as a cause.
Club rosters are patchy (indoor, beach and many smaller clubs are team-only), so some university-only players do play on where we cannot see names.
A player’s "last season" is their last season on a posted squad; gaps in the posts can make a current student look like a leaver.
Five universities, all strong programmes; small numbers per university.
gaps: UKU JustGo roster exports for every university event would cover all universities, not just the five with posted squads.
Next year’s squads, to follow the freshers named at Loughborough Beginners 2026, Bristol Beginners and SICKO.
Indoor and beach club rosters, so "not seen" stops meaning "not on grass".

findings.q: Does a club’s spirit score track whether its players come back, and does spirit differ by kind of event?
findings.hyp: Clubs with higher spirit scores keep more players; spirit is lower at the most competitive events (nationals) than at tour and university events.
findings.method: UKU's published Spirit of the Game results, 2021-22 to 2025-26: 12,014 game scores and 6,204 team-event averages (standard WFDF sheet, out of 20, shown raw). Retention: each club-season's average spirit received against the share of the club's rostered players (8+ named) seen anywhere the next season.
findings.result: Across 104 club-seasons the correlation is -0.05: clubs above the median spirit (10.3) had 76% of players back the next season, clubs below it 79%. By kind of event the averages sit in a narrow band: Junior 11.9 · Masters 10.6 · Tour 10.4 · Other club event 10.4 · Beach nationals 10.4 · Nationals 10.3 · Beach 10.3 · Regionals 10.3 · University outdoor 10.3 · Indoor qualifier 10.2 · University indoor 10.2 · University beach 10.2 · Indoor nationals 10.1.
confounds: Spirit scores cluster tightly around 10, so the differences are small compared with the noise in a weekend of games.
The clubs with 8+ named players are the better-covered clubs; small clubs are left out.
Retention is dominated by other things (club strength, division, age) that are not controlled for here.
gaps: More seasons: the game-level sheets only start in 2024-25.
Spirit at the events where we hold rosters by name, so the link can be checked player by player (who leaves a low-spirit team?).

findings.q: Do people who first appear at a club session or hat go on to play tournaments, or come back to sessions?
findings.hyp: Recreational play is a doorway: a meaningful share of people first seen at sessions and hats later play tour, nationals or above.
findings.method: People whose first record anywhere is a club session or hat (Reading Elite Jan, Deep Space pre- and off-season, SYC Charity Hat), first seen by 2025. "Tournament later" = any tour, nationals, European club, GB or club roster in a later year. "Back at sessions" = any later session or hat.
findings.result: Of 379 people first seen at a session or hat, 145 (38%) are later seen at a tournament and 120 (32%) come back to sessions or hats. first seen 2018: 44% tournament later (n 9) · first seen 2020: 37% tournament later (n 27) · first seen 2021: 43% tournament later (n 74) · first seen 2022: 26% tournament later (n 43) · first seen 2023: 45% tournament later (n 49) · first seen 2024: 38% tournament later (n 117) · first seen 2025: 35% tournament later (n 60).
confounds: The session series we hold are run by strong clubs (Reading, Deep Space) and are often invite-only, so their "recreational" players are already club players in waiting.
People first seen in a recent year have had little time to show up anywhere else.
Many tournament rosters (indoor, beach, smaller clubs) are not held by name, so "no tournament later" is an upper bound on drop-off.
gaps: Hat and league sign-ups from more clubs (KAPOW, Curve, city leagues), and beginners-course registers.
UKU membership, which would show people who play without appearing on a roster.

findings.q: Do GB youth players keep playing after their last youth squad?
findings.hyp: Most GB youth players carry on into club, and a good share make a senior or U24 squad; the drop-off after youth is smaller than for the general player.
findings.method: Players on a GB U17, U20 or U24 squad, by the year of their last youth squad (up to 2024, so everyone has had two seasons since). "Seen after" = anything in a later year; "club" = a club roster or club event; "GB again" = a later GB squad of any kind (U24 or senior after U20, senior after U24).
findings.result: Of 530 GB youth players, 243 (46%) are seen after their last youth squad, 235 (44%) at club and 94 (18%) on another GB squad. last youth squad 2010–15: 37% seen after (n 150) · last youth squad 2016–19: 52% seen after (n 231) · last youth squad 2020–24: 46% seen after (n 149).
confounds: Club rosters before 2022 are thin, so the older groups look worse than they were: their club years are partly missing.
University play is only seen for five universities from 2021-22, and youth players often go to university next.
Some youth players move abroad or play for another nation.
gaps: Junior club rosters (UKU youth championships), to see the step before GB youth too.
University rosters for every university (JustGo export).

findings.q: Does GB draw on university players, and are they already GB players when they arrive?
findings.hyp: GB players at university mostly arrive as GB youth products; university itself adds few new GB players.
findings.method: The named university squads (Bath, Exeter, KCL, Leeds, Loughborough). For each player: a GB youth squad before their first university season; any GB squad during their university years; a first GB squad only after university.
findings.result: Of 613 named university players, 32 (5%) have been on a GB squad at some point: 18 were GB youth before university, 19 were on a GB squad during university, and 4 first made GB after. Bath: 4 youth before, 4 during (of 140) · Exeter: 3 youth before, 2 during (of 95) · KCL: 1 youth before, 2 during (of 96) · Leeds: 7 youth before, 3 during (of 86) · Loughborough: 3 youth before, 8 during (of 196).
confounds: Five strong university programmes, not a sample of all universities.
Only a few seasons: players who make GB after university mostly haven’t had the chance yet.
gaps: Every university roster (JustGo export).
Two more seasons, to see who makes GB after graduating.

cannot.q: Does relative age (birth quarter within a school year) predict GB youth selection and later retention?
cannot.why: No birthdates. The youth-squad proxy is ±2 years, far coarser than the quarter needed.
cannot.need: Birth month and year on membership, or on GB squad applications.

cannot.q: Does playing at university predict staying in the club game, at every university?
cannot.why: Named squads are now in for five universities (Loughborough, Bath, KCL, Leeds, Exeter: see the finding above), from Instagram posts; every other university is still teams only.
cannot.need: UKU’s JustGo roster exports for university nationals (every player is a UKU Uni member), matched to names.

cannot.q: Do captains, coaches and committee members stay longer?
cannot.why: Roles are recorded for seven people in total (five GB youth coaches, two beach captains).
cannot.need: A roles field on squad lists, or a one-question survey: “have you captained, coached or run a club?”

cannot.q: Why do people leave: injury, cost, moving, work, lost interest, bad experience?
cannot.why: Nothing in the data records a reason.
cannot.need: An exit survey sent to the “gone while good” and the one-season-missed groups this tool can list by name.

cannot.q: Does early specialisation (ultimate only, from a young age) help or hurt?
cannot.why: No record of other sports played.
cannot.need: Survey item on other sports played to age 16.

cannot.q: Are players who drop out still playing somewhere we do not look (league, indoor, pickup, abroad)?
cannot.why: Only tracked tournaments and squad lists count as “present”.
cannot.need: UKU membership renewals, indoor league rosters, or a “are you still playing?” check sent to recent leavers.

cannot.q: Does individual performance (not team results) drive selection and retention?
cannot.why: Game stats exist for only a few events (WUCC, EUCF, some Invites).
cannot.need: This data is unlikely to ever exist at scale; player stats at Nationals would be the one realistic addition.

cannot.q: Does region or travel distance to events affect retention?
cannot.why: Home location is not recorded; clubs are the only geography.

bank.goal: Get people playing ultimate and keep them playing and investing in it, at every level and in every form: winter league, open sessions, indoor, beach, university, junior, club, masters, GB. Every question here should help find where people stop, why, and what each level needs to keep them.

status_help.answered: A finding on this page already gives a graded answer from the data we hold.
status_help.partly: We can say something from the data we hold, but a key piece is missing.
status_help.needs data: Nothing we hold can answer it yet; the data column says what would.

themes: Where and how people start playing, and which starting points lead to staying.
Where, when and for whom participation stops.
Transitions between levels: junior, university, club, GB, masters.
Grass, indoor, beach, leagues, open sessions: who plays what, and does variety keep people?
Female-matching players first (Si: questions matter five to ten times more for FMPs), and how Mixed, Women's and Open interact.
Organisers, coaches, captains, and the clubs that hold people.
Geography, hubs, travel, and what happens when events clash.
Returners, lapsed players, and what brings people back.

questions.q: Where do players start, and which starting points lead to the longest involvement?
x: What share first appear through school or junior teams, university, a club's open sessions or beginner course, a league (KAPOW, Curve), or straight onto a club tournament team?
For each starting point, how many are still playing after one, three and five years?
Does starting in a recreational setting (league, open session) lead into competitive play, or is it a separate population?
questions.data: First-seen year is held for club tournament players only. Needs JustGo membership start dates, university and junior team entries with names, and league or session sign-up lists.
questions.fq: Of the players who first appear in a given season, how many are still playing one, two and three seasons later, and does the club they started at change that?

questions.q: Do junior and school programmes produce adult players?
x: Of long-running school programmes (Badgers, Flux, Fulford), how many players reach university or club ultimate?
Do they keep playing in a different form (indoor, beach, league) rather than grass club?
Does a new school programme (Fulford) change how many juniors come through in its area?
questions.data: Junior tournament team rosters (not kept by UKU: juniors are only visible once they join), or school or club lists of past juniors by name and year.
questions.holder: Schools, junior clubs, UKU junior events team

questions.q: When did each current member start, and how long is a typical career?
x: Can the incrementing JustGo member number give an approximate first year for every member?
How does career length differ for people who started at school, university or later?
questions.data: Member ID with join date (Si can unpack the old database).

questions.q: At what age do people start, and does starting later mean a shorter or longer time in the sport?
x: Is there a meaningful group starting after university, in their late 20s or 30s?
Do late starters stay mainly in recreational play?
questions.data: Year of birth (or age band) with member ID and join date.

questions.q: How many players come back each season, and where is churn highest?
x: Retention by division, club strength, Quality band and years in the sport.
Is the first or second season the biggest cliff?
Does churn differ for FMPs and MMPs?
questions.data: Club tournament rosters (held). FMP/MMP for every player would allow the gender split everywhere; it is partial now.
questions.fq: How many club players come back the next season, and does it differ by division?

questions.q: Is dropout concentrated at the bottom (weaker clubs, lower Quality) or spread across every level?
x: Do lower-Quality players leave the sport, or only leave grass for indoor, beach or leagues?
Is there a club or team size below which players drift away?
questions.data: Answered for grass club play. Whether leavers are still playing elsewhere needs indoor and beach rosters and league lists.
questions.fq: Is dropout concentrated at the bottom (weak clubs, low Quality) or does it happen at every level?

questions.q: Do players who only play one kind of event drop out more than players who play a full season?
x: Is the link the same for Tour-only, Nationals-only and invite-only players?
Does adding an indoor or beach event to a grass season change the chance of coming back?
questions.data: Answered for grass events. Indoor and beach rosters would show whether other formats count too.
questions.fq: Do players who only play one kind of event drop out more than players who play the full season?

questions.q: How much playing keeps people playing?
x: Does the number of events in a season predict coming back?
Is there a sweet spot, or does too much play (several divisions and surfaces) lead to burnout or injury?
questions.data: The lower end is answered for grass. The burnout end needs multi-surface rosters and ideally an injury question in a survey.
questions.fq: Does the number of events a player plays in a season predict whether they come back?

questions.q: Do players leave soon after their best season, or play on past their peak?
x: Who left while still good, and why?
Who has a long tail, and what kept them?
questions.data: Why they left needs asking: the lists are on the finding.
questions.fq: Do players leave soon after their best season, or play on past their peak?

questions.q: Why do people stop?
x: Injury, cost, moving, work, family, losing interest, a bad experience, their team folding, not being selected?
Do the reasons differ by level, age and FMP/MMP?
What would have kept them?
questions.data: A short exit or lapsed-member survey sent to people who did not renew, and to the 'who to ask' lists on this page.

questions.q: When someone disappears from the grass club data, have they actually stopped playing?
x: What share are still at indoor, beach, leagues, open sessions or pickup, or playing abroad?
Is leaving competitive grass a loss to the sport or just a change of format?
questions.data: Indoor and beach rosters, league and session sign-ups, and membership renewals (a renewing member is still involved).

questions.q: Does university ultimate feed the club game, or is it where many people stop?
x: What share of university players play club ultimate during or after university?
Why are there around 150 registered at Loughborough but far fewer Loughborough players at outdoor club events?
Is university play mostly social, and is that fine (part of the recreational base)?
questions.data: Named squads for five universities (Loughborough, Bath, KCL, Leeds, Exeter) from Instagram posts, 2022-23 to 2025-26. Every other university is teams only; UKU JustGo exports for university events would cover them all.
questions.fq: Do university players who also play club while at university stay in the sport after they graduate?

questions.q: What happens to GB youth players?
x: How many U17, U20 and U24 players reach a senior grass team, and when do they stop?
Are U20-only players (selected on athleticism, still deciding whether they like it) a group that drops out more?
Does a GB youth cap predict staying in the sport longer than club players of the same standard?
questions.data: Pathway and retention are on the GB programme page; ages are estimated. Birth year would make it exact.
questions.fq: How old are GB youth products when they reach a senior squad, and when they stop playing?

questions.q: Do training squads develop players, or select players who were going to improve anyway?
x: Do training-squad players improve more than similar players who were not on one?
Is the effect only for elite-club training squads (Deep Space into Clapham, Spice into Iceni)?
Does being on a training squad and not making the team lead to leaving?
questions.data: Training-squad lists for more clubs and years; a fair comparison group (similar Quality, no training squad).

questions.q: When players switch division, where do they go, and do they stay?
x: Open to Mixed, Mixed to Women's, and back: what changes for the player?
Is a switch a way to keep playing (for example after not being selected)?
questions.data: Held for grass club play.
questions.fq: When players switch division, where do they go, what happens to their Quality, and do they stay?

questions.q: Does changing club keep people in the sport, and does the direction matter?
x: Is moving to a weaker team the first step out, or a way to keep playing?
Which clubs do players move to when they leave a club, and why?
questions.data: Why they moved needs asking.
questions.fq: Do players who change clubs stay in the sport longer or shorter than players who stay put, and does the direction of the move matter?

questions.q: Is the end of a four-year international cycle a point where experienced players stop?
x: Do GB players leave after a World Championships more than in other years?
Do they move to masters, coaching or organising instead?
questions.data: Senior GB rosters before 2010 (Si: senior squads go back to the 1990s) and coaching or admin roles.
questions.fq: Do GB players stay in the sport more than club players of the same standard?

questions.q: Who plays each form of ultimate?
x: Who plays beach, and is it mostly a regional thing (people who live near the coast)?
Are indoor players the same people as grass club players, or a different group?
What share of league and open-session players also play tournaments? (Max's sense: about 20 to 30% at KAPOW.)
questions.data: Indoor and beach results are held at team level; rosters by name would link them to players. League sign-ups from organisers (Lucas for KAPOW; Curve).

questions.q: Do players who play more than one form stay longer?
x: Does playing beach keep people longer?
Does indoor keep people in the sport over the winter?
Is cross-surface play good for retention or a burnout risk?
questions.data: Indoor and beach rosters by name, or member IDs on event entries.

questions.q: How big is the recreational base, and is it big enough?
x: What share of people who play are mainly social (Si's guess: about 30% would make a healthy pyramid)?
Do leagues and open sessions hold on to people who would otherwise stop (the 'I just like playing once a week' group)?
What do recreational players need that they are not getting?
questions.data: League and session sign-ups by name over several seasons, matched to tournament play; a short survey on what people want from playing.

questions.q: What does each club offer, and does the offer change how many people it keeps?
x: Which clubs run open sessions, beginner courses, leagues, youth sections, masters sides, indoor and beach teams?
Do clubs with a wider offer keep more players or grow faster?
questions.data: Club pages already show grass, indoor, beach, youth and masters teams. Sessions, courses and leagues need a short club survey or the clubs' own listings.

questions.q: Which events draw which players, and what does each level of event need?
x: Which events attract the strongest players, and which attract newer ones?
Are there players who only ever play one particular event each year?
questions.data: Held for grass; indoor and beach need rosters.
questions.fq: Which events draw the strongest players, and how far apart are they?

questions.q: Is every churn and pathway pattern different for FMPs?
x: Retention, first-season cliff, return after a gap, and moves, all split by FMP and MMP.
Where do FMPs stop, and is it at different points from MMPs?
questions.data: FMP/MMP is known for Women's and some Mixed rosters; needs a gender marker for every player (JustGo) to split every finding.

questions.q: Does Mixed draw players away from Women's?
x: How many FMPs play both, and does playing both change how long they stay?
Would splitting the competitions so everyone could play both help, or do players sensibly pick one?
Do Women's teams fold or shrink when a strong Mixed team appears nearby?
questions.data: Cross-division play is visible on grass rosters we hold; indoor and beach rosters and a gender marker would complete it.

questions.q: Who are the people who keep others playing?
x: Can we find the 'pillars' (people like Ho Lam or Cheska) from how many players they have played with, coached or brought in?
What happens to a club's numbers when a key organiser steps back?
Are those people known, thanked and supported?
questions.data: The teammate graph is held (Connections page). Coaching, captaincy and organiser roles from JustGo and clubs would make it much sharper.

questions.q: Do masters players go on to start clubs, coach juniors or organise?
x: Is there a link between masters play (Zimmer, grand masters) and junior coaching or new clubs (Epsom, Bristol)?
Does protecting masters competition keep these people connected to the sport?
questions.data: Masters rosters (partly held) plus coach, admin and club-founder roles.

questions.q: Do captains, coaches and committee members stay longer?
x: Does taking on a role extend a player's involvement?
Does a club with more people in roles keep more players?
questions.data: Role lists by year (some rosters already mark captains and coaches).

questions.q: What does a club that keeps its players look like?
x: Size, number of teams, offer, intake each year, turnover, strength.
Do clubs that take in a large new group each year keep them?
questions.data: Club pages show retention and flows for clubs with rosters. Clubs' own kit lists and session lists (as Reading has) make this much stronger.
questions.fq: Does the quality a club gains or loses through moves in one season predict how its rating changes the next?

questions.q: Does where people live affect whether they play and keep playing?
x: Are there areas with players but no club?
Does travel distance to events predict dropping out?
Is the Midlands really an indoor hub?
questions.data: Members' locations, kept by UKU and joined by member ID; only area-level totals need to leave UKU.

questions.q: How many people are affected when two events clash?
x: How many players and teams are shared between any two events (for example Mixed Nationals and a masters event, or U17s and European Club Masters)?
Whom does a clash really hurt: coaches who are also masters players, junior teams, FMPs who play two divisions?
Which weekends are safe to use when venues are lost (for example to drought)?
questions.data: Shared players can be counted for grass events with rosters now; indoor, beach, junior and masters rosters would complete it.

questions.q: Does the shape of the season help or hurt participation?
x: Do long gaps between events lose players?
Does a crowded calendar push people to pick one division or surface?
questions.data: Event calendar by year (held for many events) linked to rosters across all formats.

questions.q: Who comes back after a long gap, and what brings them back?
x: How many people return in their late 30s and 40s after years away?
Do they come back through masters, leagues, their children, or their old club?
Do they stay once they return?
questions.data: Returns after one or more missed seasons are visible from 2010; longer gaps need older rosters and JustGo history.

questions.q: After a missed season, who comes back and who is gone for good?
x: About a quarter come back after a missed season: what is different about them?
Is a message or invitation at the right moment enough to bring some back?
questions.data: The pattern is held; the why needs a survey of the 'missed one season' list.
questions.fq: How many club players come back the next season, and does it differ by division?

questions.q: Why does such a big group appear for the first time at GB masters?
x: Are they mostly people who played GB before 2010, when our data starts (Si's reading)?
Or are some genuinely new to GB, coming back through masters?
questions.data: Senior GB rosters 1998 to 2010 (UKU has them).

questions.q: Does relative age (birth month within the school year) affect who gets selected and who stays?
x: Are GB youth squads skewed to players born early in the school year?
Do late-born players who are not selected drop out more?
questions.data: Date or month of birth for junior and GB youth players.

questions.q: Does playing other sports, or specialising early in ultimate, help or hurt long-term involvement?
x: Do players who came from other sports stay longer or shorter?
Do juniors who play only ultimate burn out earlier?
questions.data: A short survey question on sporting background.

questions.q: Does individual performance, not just team results, drive selection and staying in the sport?
x: Do players who stand out on weaker teams get picked up and stay?
Is Quality (which is built from team results) missing good players on weak teams?
questions.data: Individual stats (for example from tournament scoring apps) or coach ratings.

questions.q: Does playing club while at university keep people in the sport after graduating?
x: Is it the club play itself, or are the players who join a club already the committed ones?
Does a university team entering club events (Open Tour, indoor qualifiers, Lemmings Luau) do the same job as students joining a club?
Is the effect different for FMPs and MMPs, and for Mixed, Women’s and Open?
questions.data: Named university squads (five universities so far) linked to club rosters and events.
questions.fq: Do university players who also play club while at university stay in the sport after they graduate?

questions.q: Where do university players go after graduating, and which clubs take in which universities?
x: Do graduates join the club nearest the university, or the club in the city they move to?
Do the strongest university programmes feed particular top clubs (Bath to Bristol and Clapham, Loughborough to Ka-Pow!, Deep Space and Solent)?
How many of a university’s squad are already club players when they arrive (Leeds women with SMOG and Horizon)?
questions.data: Named university squads plus club rosters after graduation; destinations are thin until more club rosters are held.
questions.fq: Do university players who also play club while at university stay in the sport after they graduate?

questions.q: Do freshers who start at a beginners event (Loughborough Beginners, Bristol Beginners, SICKO) end up on university squads, and then in the club game?
x: What share of a freshers’ intake is on a university squad by the spring?
Do the universities that run their own beginners events keep more of their freshers?
Is the first year the main drop-off point for university players?
questions.data: Beginners-event team lists for 2025 and 2026 are held (Loughborough, Bath, KCL). Needs the same universities’ squads next season to follow them.

questions.q: Are players on lower university teams (3s, 4s, 5s) the ones who stop, and do big clubs like Loughborough keep their lower teams playing?
x: Does moving up from the 4s or 5s to the 1s predict staying in the sport?
How big is the drop between a university’s 1s and its lower teams in being seen again?
questions.data: Team number is held on every named university squad; same five universities.
questions.fq: Do university players who also play club while at university stay in the sport after they graduate?

questions.q: Does a club’s spirit score track whether its players come back?
x: Do players leave low-spirit teams more often than high-spirit ones?
Is it the team’s own behaviour (what it receives) or its generosity (what it gives) that matters?
Does spirit at a player’s first events predict whether they stay?
questions.data: UKU spirit results 2021-22 to 2025-26 (club-season averages) against next-season retention from rosters; game-level sheets only from 2024-25.
questions.fq: Does a club’s spirit score track whether its players come back, and does spirit differ by kind of event?

questions.q: Does spirit change with the kind of event, and over the years?
x: Are nationals and tour scored differently from indoor and university events?
Are the categories (rules, fouls, fair-mindedness, attitude, communication) driving the differences?
Has the average moved since the WFDF sheet was standardised?
questions.data: UKU spirit results by event kind and season (Spirit page).
questions.fq: Does a club’s spirit score track whether its players come back, and does spirit differ by kind of event?

questions.q: How big is the recreational population (sessions, hats, leagues, beginners events), and how does it connect to the club game?
x: How many people only ever play recreationally?
Which recreational events feed club teams, and which are a world of their own?
What share of club players also play recreationally in the same year?
questions.data: Named sessions and hats for a few series (Elite Jan, Deep Space, SYC Charity Hat), beginners events for three universities. Needs KAPOW, Curve and other league sign-ups, and club session lists.

questions.q: What kinds of event are run each year, and how is that changing?
x: Are beginners events and hats growing or shrinking?
Is indoor the biggest part of the calendar by count, and does it convert into outdoor club play?
Which regions run the most community events?
questions.data: UKU events calendar 2022–2026 (Engagement page). Club-run events not listed with UKU are missing.

defs:
present in a season  = any appearance that year (club event, club roster list, GB squad, overseas club)
  on a club roster     = Club first/second team, Masters side, Secondary team (training players excluded)
  left after year Y    = present in Y, never seen in any later year we hold (2026 is the current season, so 2025 leavers are
                         provisional; "left" really means "not seen at the events and squads we track")
  back next season     = present in Y and in Y+1 (any club, any format)
  evidence grade       strong = large n and a clear gap that survives the obvious split; suggestive = clear gap, small n or an
                       obvious selection story; weak = pattern visible but could easily be noise or selection
